title: Pricing the Context Window: A Unified Write–Read Theory for Token-Efficient Agent Memory
content: The finite context window of a foundation model is the central scarce resource of an LLM agent harness: every token admitted costs money and latency and, beyond a point, degrades the answer. We argue that agent memory is an investment problem. What is written determines the retrieval problem the agent will later face, and the distribution of future retrievals determines what is worth writing. We formalize this as the joint optimization of a write policy (what is stored, at which resolution, with which shortcuts) and a read policy (what is loaded for a query) in one numeraire, with context tokens priced by a shadow price λ. We claim no novelty for the ingredients (value of information, submodular selection, rate–distortion, MDL, predictive information); The contribution is the coupling and what it implies: (i) a depth law in which optimal graph-traversal depth depends on token price, branching, signal decay and scorer quality; (ii) a write criterion measured against query-time re-derivation, with an explicit externality of writes on retrieval depth; (iii) a lower bound on the information content of any predictively sufficient memory; and (iv) thresholds for resolution levels, shortcuts, a cached core, query planning, refresh and indexing. Results are stated as propositions under explicit assumptions, design rules, and eight testable hypotheses. None is yet empirically validated.
